assign.outcome: **`/framework/ai/<day>/` (and any task inside it) reproduced and fixed: it was genuinely unreachable below 64em while routed.** `.page-catalog-pages` measured `clientHeight:0` against a `scrollHeight` of 8725 (390px) / 5311 (720px) on a real day page — confirmed via a Playwright probe against the dev server, no shell/no browser workaround needed. Root cause matched ext/catalog's own diagnosis exactly: ai.css's `<64em` media query gave `.ai-index-rail` `max-height: none` unconditionally, and the `shrink:0` rail's full natural height (26237px) claimed the whole column the moment catalog.css turns `.page-catalog` into a column below 64em, leaving nothing for the sibling region. Fixed in public/framework/ext/AITask/ai.css: scoped the mobile rule to `.page-catalog:has(> .page-catalog-pages > .page:is(.active-page, .active-ancestor)) > .ai-index-rail` — the identical routed test the desktop board-mode rule already keys off — and reused the desktop default's own bound verbatim (`flex: 0 0 min(34em, 45%); max-height: 100dvh`) rather than inventing a new number: flex-basis and max-height both resolve against whichever axis is currently main, so the same declaration that bounds the rail's WIDTH in the row layout bounds its HEIGHT once the column takes over. Verified with analyze() across 390/720/1280/3440 × routed/unrouted on /framework/ai/2026-08-16/ and /framework/ai/ (8/8 clean) plus 10 more catalog() callers × 4 widths (40/40 clean) — unreachable/zero-size/gutter all absent everywhere this fix could reach. Two unrelated pre-existing findings surfaced by the sweep, confirmed via git stash to predate this change and left alone as out-of-fence: a low gutter on /framework/core/Page/'s table (matches ext/catalog/readme.md's recorded rail-overshoot) and a new high gutter on /framework/ext/catalog/'s own .demo-app-pages, reported not fixed. Recorded in public/framework/ext/AITask/readme.md's Traps.
